purpose: Teach: リサイタル/霊感/傍観/重き/ダブリン/打席/スタメン/チューニング

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、リサイタル、絶対、聴きに行ったわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When we were young, Dad was absolutely serious about us going to his recitals. Every single one.
lines.style: Gentle opening, like reaching back through decades. Warm, measured pace. Slight lift on 'remember' — checking that she's there with him. Voice settles into fondness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、霊感、絶対、強い時期、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. When I was young, I really did have a strong intuition about things — you remember that, don't you? I was so certain about so much.
lines.style: Soft, almost marveling at the memory. Reaches back gently, then a small laugh at her own certainty. Voice trails slightly — she's surprised by her own past intensity.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、傍観、絶対、せず、絶対、皆を助けたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Your father — he never sat on the sidelines, Gran. He really did help everyone around him. You remember that?
lines.style: Firmer now, with quiet conviction. A light emphasis on 'never' — defending an old memory. Still warm, but the voice carries a small weight of admiration.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、家族に、絶対、重き、絶対、を、絶対、置いていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: That's right. Your grandfather — he put such weight on family. He really did, you know. Do you remember?
lines.style: Warm and certain, like she's handing him back something he gave her. Soft but steady. The voice holds the memory like it's fragile and precious.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ダブリン、絶対、の、絶対、お話、絶対、本で、絶対、読んだぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your father — he read all those stories about Dublin in books. Do you remember that, Gran?
lines.style: Slightly wistful, reaching for a specific detail. Gentle pace, like he's trying to hold onto it. Voice softens on 'Dublin' — almost romantically.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、野球の、絶対、打席、絶対、頑張ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes — your grandfather worked so hard at baseball, didn't he? Those at-bats. He really gave everything to it. Do you remember?
lines.style: Warm recognition, like she's suddenly seeing it again. A small smile in the voice. The pace is gentle but engaged — she's right there with him in the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、地域の野球チームの、絶対、スタメン、絶対、だったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: That's true. He was the starter for the local team, your grandfather. Right from the beginning. Do you remember?
lines.style: Quiet pride settling in. A steady, grounded voice. Light emphasis on 'starter' — he's marking something important. Slightly slower pace, like he's making sure she hears it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、ラジオの、絶対、チューニング、絶対、丁寧にしてくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: He was so careful with the radio, you know — the way he'd tune it. Your grandfather had such a gentle touch with those small things. Don't you remember?
lines.style: Tender and specific, lingering on the image. Voice becomes almost intimate — she's seeing his hands. Slight breath between clauses, like she's lost in the memory for a moment.
